Jayachandra 'was defeated and killed at the Battle of Chandawar in 1194. The Ghurids then sacked Varanasi.' The dossier ends in 1194; Cliopatria keeps the shape to 1201 and starts its Ghurid shape over this land only in 1202 (the Ghurid 1192 shape has 0 of its 852 cells, the 1205 shape 560), so 1195-1201 should be drawn as Ghurid or as the rump of Harishchandra (c. 1194-1197, a 1197 Kotwa inscription with sovereign titles; Ghurid-vassal theory) by the ghurid-dynasty dossier. Unchanged outline, years cut.

region.text: Varanasi (Kashi), where Chandradeva 'likely took' the city from the Kalachuris

ledger.note: c. 1085: Chandradeva founds the Gahadavala kingdom at Varanasi. The page has him 'established a sovereign kingdom sometime before 1090, after the decline of the Kalachuri power' and 'declared independence sometime before 1089 CE' (ruler list c. 1089-1103; infobox 'Established 1072'); 'Chandradeva likely captured this territory from them' (the Kalachuris held the Varanasi area). Cliopatria starts the row in 1085; the year is a bridge to it (confidence 1). The founding land is the Varanasi (Kashi) land taken from the Kalachuris of Tripuri (counterpart changed from gurjara-pratihara-dynasty in the repair of 2026-10-19, which also limits the 1090 event to Kosala and the 1093 event to Kannauj): the later inscriptions add Kosala (1090) and Kannauj (1093).

region.text: Uttara Koshala, the area around Ayodhya

ledger.note: 1090: Kosala. The 1090 Chandrawati inscription says Chandradeva 'protected the sacred places of Kashi (Varanasi), Kushika (Kannauj), Uttara Koshala' (the area around Ayodhya) and Indrasthaniyaka (identity unknown; Delhi is a scholars' guess the page rejects). The inscription attests the land by 1090; the page dates no conquest, so 1090 is the attestation (confidence 2) and the gain is limited to the Ayodhya area, since Kashi is the founding land and Kannauj is the 1093 event (repair of 2026-10-19). The page's lead has the kingdom arise 'after the decline of the Kalachuri power', hence the counterpart.

1093: Kannauj. 'The Gahadavalas occupied Kanyakubja after the Gurjara-Pratihara descendants of Devapala were destroyed, according to 1093 and 1100 CE Chandrawati inscriptions' (Gahadavala page); the 1090 inscription already names Kushika (Kannauj), so 1093 is the attestation and not the conquest. The page names no holder of Kannauj in 1036-1093 (gurjara-pratihara-dynasty ends in 1036; the Govindachandra page's 'Gadhipuradhipati Gopala' is one reading of the 1114 Pali claim, not a dated holder), so the counterpart is nobody (changed from gurjara-pratihara-dynasty in the repair of 2026-10-19).

region.text: the rest of Cliopatria's 1085 outline short of Bihar and the Yamuna-Sone land: the Doab, Awadh and Prayaga between Kashi, Kushika and Koshala, and the Himalayan rim

ledger.note: c. 1100 (bridge): the land between the three named centres joins. The 1100 Chandrawati inscription is the last dated attestation of Chandradeva's kingdom (Gahadavala page) and the page puts the furthest north-west inscription at Rahin in Etawah district; no page names any other town, border or conquest. Cliopatria draws the whole outline from 1085, and the repair of 2026-10-19 splits it so that the ledger carries the growth. This event is the part that no page explains: 465 cells, being the Uttar Pradesh land between the Varanasi, Ayodhya and Kannauj discs (345 cells; the Doab, Awadh and Prayaga of the 'Kashi-Kushika-Koshala' land), the Himalayan rim (Nepal 74, Uttarakhand 44 cells, which neither page mentions: 'Nepal, Himalaya, Uttarakhand: not on page') and 2 cells in Madhya Pradesh. Confidence 1; the Bihar part and the Kalachuri land of 1120 are separate events.

1104: the Ghaznavids take Kannauj. 'the Gahadavalas lost Kanyakubja somewhere between 1104 CE and 1105 CE' (Govindachandra page: the same words); Madanapala (identified with 'Malhi') was held until a ransom was paid.

by 1109: Govindachandra, then prince, wins Kannauj back. 'His princely inscriptions show he had restored Gahadavala power in Kanyakubja and its surroundings by 1109 CE' (he led a war to recover it); a Ghaznavid peace treaty followed his campaigns (undated on the Gahadavala page).

region.text: the Kalachuri land between the Yamuna and the Sone, beyond the discs already held

ledger.note: 1120: Kalachuri land between the Yamuna and the Sone. Govindachandra adopted Kalachuri titles in 1120, 'presumably a way of celebrating his victory over the Kalachuris'; the annexed territory 'must have been located in the region between the Yamuna and the Sone rivers' (a reading of the page, not a boundary). Region corrected in the repair of 2026-10-19 to the Mirzapur disc without the land already held, so that it is not counted twice.

region.text: the part of present-day Bihar that Govindachandra 'controlled', bounded in the north-east by the Burhi Gandak

ledger.note: c. 1124 (bridge): Govindachandra holds part of Bihar. 'In the east, Govindachandra controlled a part of the present-day Bihar' and 'His easternmost inscription has been found at Maner in Patna district' (1124 on the page); 'In the north-east, his kingdom was probably bounded by the Burhi Gandak River'. The page does not say when the land was won; the Palas invaded 'sometime before 1109' and the conflict 'seems to have happened over control of present-day western Bihar' (Gahadavala page). The first dated evidence inside his reign (c. 1114-1155) is used, confidence 1. Added in the repair of 2026-10-19: Cliopatria's shape holds 111 Bihar cells from 1085, 29 years before the reign.

1140s: the Pala-Gahadavala conflict revives over western Bihar. 'The Pala-Gahadavala conflict revived in the 1140s CE over western Bihar'; 'it is possible that Govindachandra invaded the Pala kingdom sometime around 1146 CE', reaching Munger (Govindachandra page). A marriage alliance (Kumaradevi of Bodh Gaya) 'probably followed'.

region.text: the cells that leave Cliopatria's shape in 1152

ledger.note: 1152: Cliopatria's shape trims 24 cells (and adds 16) against 1085. No page names any of them (confidence 1); the large Bihar loss is the c. 1155 event.

c. 1155: the Bihar contest ends with the reign. Govindachandra 'controlled part of present-day Bihar, but lost the eastern territory by the end of his reign' (his last inscription is of 1154; the list has c. 1155). The year is the end of the reign (confidence 1).

region.text: the Bihar part of the Cliopatria shape, the territory lost 'by the end of his reign'

ledger.note: c. 1155: the Bihar land is lost. 'However, the Pala inscriptions in this area indicate that he lost this territory by the end of his reign' (Govindachandra page; his last inscription is of 1154, the list has c. 1155), 'this territory' being the part of Bihar he controlled; Munger 'later came under the control of Madanapala'. Region corrected in the repair of 2026-10-19 from the 8 cells that Cliopatria trims in 1152 to the whole Bihar part of its shape (105 cells), which Cliopatria keeps to 1201. The page does not name the new holder; the Pala shape of 1152-1168 is Bihar. The year is the end of the reign (confidence 2).
1194: the Ghurids defeat Jayachandra. 'Jayachandra was defeated and killed at the Battle of Chandawar in 1194. The Ghurids then sacked Varanasi.'

1194: the kingdom falls. Harishchandra (c. 1194-1197) follows with a 1197 Kotwa inscription claiming sovereign titles, in tension with the theory that he was a Ghurid vassal; the dynasty 'completely ceased to exist' when Jayachandra's successors were defeated by the Delhi Sultanate (undated; Iltutmish r. 1211-1236).

1194: the Gahadavala kingdom ends at Chandawar. Infobox 'Succeeded by: Ghurid dynasty and Delhi Sultanate', 'Disestablished 1237' (a 1237 inscription mentions Adakkamalla of the Gahadavala family, uncertain). The rump of Harishchandra to 1197 and the later Gahadavala remnant are not drawn.

wars.name: Gahadavala-Ghaznavid wars
wars.outcome: The Ghaznavids take Kannauj between 1104 and 1105 and hold Madanapala to ransom; Govindachandra restores Gahadavala power there by 1109 and a peace treaty follows; Vijayachandra repulses a Ghaznavid invasion 'sometime before 1164'.
wars.note: Kumaradevi's inscription praises Govindachandra for 'protecting Varanasi from the wicked Turushkas', yet 'no Ghaznavid advance on Varanasi is recorded' (Govindachandra page).

wars.name: Pala-Gahadavala wars
wars.outcome: The Palas invade before 1109, possibly in revenge for Chandradeva's expansion; the conflict 'revived in the 1140s CE over western Bihar'; Govindachandra possibly reaches Munger c. 1146 and a marriage alliance follows; the eastern part of his Bihar land is lost by the end of his reign.

notes:
WHAT THE ROW IS. Cliopatria's Gahadavala shape (1085-1201, three shapes of 852-860 cells) is one outline of the Kashi-Kannauj-Kosala heart (Uttar Pradesh 624, Bihar 105-111, Nepal 74-79, Uttarakhand 40-44, Madhya Pradesh 5-7) that fits both pages except for its Himalayan rim (Nepal, Uttarakhand), which neither page mentions. START: 'sometime before 1090' / 'before 1089' on the page, infobox 1072; Cliopatria 1085 is used (confidence 1). END: the page gives Chandawar in 1194, Harishchandra c. 1194-1197 (a 1197 inscription with sovereign titles, in tension with the Ghurid-vassal theory) and an infobox end of 1237 (Adakkamalla, possibly Harishchandra's successor, 'not certain'); Cliopatria ends in 1201 and starts the Ghurid shape over the land in 1202. 1194 is used and 1195-1201 are left to the ghurid-dynasty dossier (or to a rump dossier if a gap-filler wants one). Disagreements: the Kannauj gain is 1093/1100 (Chandrawati inscriptions) while the 1090 inscription already names Kannauj; Govindachandra's accession is 1109-1114 and the list's c. 1114 is used; the Gahadavala page speaks of a Pala conflict 'in the 1140s', the Govindachandra page of an invasion 'possibly c. 1146'.

PAGES: Gahadavala dynasty, Govindachandra (a disambiguation, empty, opened by mistake) and Govindachandra (Gahadavala dynasty); the budget was 1-2 pages. Not covered: Jayachandra (no page opened), the Sena invasion, the Tomara and Chahamana frontier near Delhi, the Chandela frontier (the Chandela dossier has a 1085 bridge loss of 28 cells to the Gahadavalas; 'Relations were friendly' on the Govindachandra page), the Turushka-danda tax (undated). Counterparts without dossiers: Kalachuri of Tripuri (suggested slug kalachuri-of-tripuri; the dossier kalachuris-of-mahishmati is a different Kalachuri line). Gazetteer names: Ayodhya, Varanasi, Patna, Mirzapur exist; Kannauj/Kanyakubja and Chandawar are used as coordinates and are wanted as places.

REPAIR OF 2026-10-19 (reviewer findings; both Govindachandra and Gahadavala pages re-read). (1) Bihar: the Bihar part of Cliopatria's shape (111 cells) is no longer drawn from 1085; a gain c. 1124 (the Maner inscription; the page never says when the land was won, confidence 1) and a loss c. 1155 of the whole Bihar part (105 cells, confidence 2) replace the 8-cell loss, and the keyframes 1155 and 1192 drop Bihar. (2) The 1085 shape is now staged: Varanasi 1085-1089 (127 cells in the 110 km disc), plus the Ayodhya area 1090, plus Kannauj 1093, a c. 1100 bridge (confidence 1) adding the rest of the outline between the named centres together with the Himalayan rim, the Kalachuri land 1120 and Bihar c. 1124. This is the reviewer's first option; the 1090 and 1093 dates are inscription attestations, so a reader who prefers the second option (the whole outline from 1085) can drop the 1090, 1093 and 1100 events and keyframes. (3) Counterparts: the founding and the 1090 Kosala are from the Kalachuris of Tripuri (the page's 'after the decline of the Kalachuri power'); Kannauj 1093 is from nobody (the holder in 1036-1093 is not named; the Rashtrakutas of Kannauj are 'Govindachandra's feudatories' on the page, not dated holders), which also stops the mismatch with gurjara-pratihara-dynasty's 1036 dissolve. (4) The Govindachandra disambiguation entry and the 1206 war end were already corrected by the reviewer. (5) Not done (thin, for gap-fillers): the 1085 year, the Sena-Gahadavala conflicts. Mirrors: pala-empire has no gain of the Bihar land in 1155 (its 1147 note: Madanapala took Munger from the Gahadavalas, 1145-1147 on the Govindachandra page); chandela-kingdom /ledger/9 (1085 loss to the Gahadavalas) has no Gahadavala gain.
